questions.question: Distinguish between generalized and specialized transduction. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Distinguish between generalized and specialized transduction
  • The process of genetic recombination occurs when a bacteriophage (phage virus) transfers
  • DNA from one bacterium to another.
  • Generalized Transduction
  • ▪ Occurs during the lytic cycle of a phage.
  • ▪ Any random gene from the donor bacterium may be transferred.
  • ▪ Happens when the phage mistakenly packages bacterial DNA into its
  • capsid.
  • ▪ Occurs frequently in the phage life cycle.
  • Specialized Transduction
  • ▪ Occurs during the lysogenic cycle of a temperate phage.
  • ▪ Only specific genes near the phage integration site are transferred.
  • ▪ Happens when the phage incorrectly excises from the bacterial
  • chromosome, taking adjacent genes with it.
  • ▪ Occurs rarely compared to generalized transduction.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write short notes on terrestrial and aquatic forms of algae. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Write short notes on terrestrial and aquatic forms of algae
  • Aquatic Algae: Found in water bodies such as ponds, lakes, rivers, and seas. May be free-
  • floating (planktonic), swimming (motile), or attached to rocks or submerged surfaces. Include
  • both freshwater and marine forms.(Give any one example for each).
  • Terrestrial Algae: Occur on land, particularly in moist or damp habitats such as soil, tree
  • trunks, rocks, and walls. Based on habitat, terrestrial algae are divided into: a. Saprophytic
  • Forms: Grow on damp soil, rocks, or tree surfaces.eg; Vaucheria b. Cryptophytic Forms: Grow
  • Page3
  • inside the soil and contribute to nitrogen fixation and soil fertility . Examples: Nostoc,
  • Anabaena, Trentipohlia etc) Symbiotic Forms: Some algae form symbiotic associations with
  • fungi to produce lichens, which can grow on rocks, tree bark, and walls.
  • (Examples can also be considered for marks)

questions.question: Describe the main features of the vegetative structure in Chara. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the main features of the vegetative structure in Chara.
  • • The thallus is macroscopic, erect, and plant-like.
  • • It is clearly differentiated into rhizoids, main axis, and branches.
  • • The main axis has nodes and internodes
  • • Branches of unlimited growth and limited growth
  • • Cell wall made of cellulose, encrusted with calcium carbonate, giving a stony texture.
  • • Discoid Chloroplast with pyrenoids storing starch
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Describe the main features of a Cladophora cell. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the main features of a Cladophora cell
  • • Each cell is large and multinucleated (coenocytic).
  • • The cell wall is thick, composed of outer chitin, middle pectic, and inner cellulosic
  • layers.
  • • Reticulate chloroplast with several pyrenoids
  • • The cytoplasm forms a thin lining along the inner wall and encloses a large central
  • vacuole.

questions.question: Compare and contrast viruses, viroids and prions. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Compare and contrast viruses, viroids and prions
  • Page4
  • Viruses, viroids and prions are acellular infectious agents that cannot reproduce on their own.
  • They depend entirely on living host cells for multiplication.
  • Viruses
  • • Non-cellular particles made of nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) enclosed in a protein coat
  • (capsid). Some have an envelope and spikes.
  • • Ultramicroscopic, about 20–300 nm.
  • • No cytoplasm or organelles.
  • • Obligate intracellular parasites
  • • Hosts: Infect plants, animals, and bacteria (bacteriophages). Examples: Tobacco
  • Mosaic Virus (TMV),

questions.question: What are the advantages and disadvantages of water blooms? / [CO3] [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• What are the advantages and disadvantages of water blooms?
  • (Liberal valuation. Anything related to algal blooms can be considered.
  • Advantages Disadvantages
  • Nitrogen-fixing algae increase fertility Oxygen depletion due to decomposition of
  • dense blooms
  • Serve as food for birds and aquatic animals. Produce toxins (e.g., microcystins,
  • anatoxins) harmful to life.
  • Indicate nutrient pollution — useful for
  • environmental monitoring.
  • Cause bad odour and taste in water.
  • Clog water filters, irrigation channels, and
  • fish gills.
  • Block sunlight, reducing photosynthesis in
  • submerged plants.
